review_notes: I read the whole file and applied only the repeated-proof-machinery rubric. I did not open any related source files. The proofs are mostly one-line `ext x; rw [mem_.., mem_.., succ_le_iff_of_not_isMax / lt_succ_iff_of_not_isMax]` scripts, or short `rw` chains through earlier lemmas. These are routine unfolding and are too short to count as nontrivial repeated reasoning. The `NoMaxOrder` lemmas are thin wrappers around the `_of_not_isMax` lemmas. The `to_dual` attribute already removes the succ/pred duplication. The only similar structure is the `by_cases IsMax/IsMin` empty-interval split, which appears in `Ico_succ_left_eq_Ioo` and `Icc_succ_pred_eq_Ioo`. The two branches prove different things, so a shared helper would not clearly improve either proof. The `simp [or_and_left, ...]` scripts in the `insert_Icc_*` lemmas look alike but have different hypotheses and closing tactics. I could not run Lean, so I could not check whether a unification would compile. Based on reading alone, I found no justified finding.
